chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them, from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"For the one who does not menstruate like her [i.e., does not have regular menses], there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her."

key_terms.تَحْبَلُ: She menstruates (literally: she becomes pregnant/capable of bearing)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman who does not menstruate?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'iddah for non-menstruating women is clarified by comparing them to those who do not conceive, establishing a fixed three-month period rather than relying on menstrual cycles. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the waiting period of children, menopausal women, and those with irregular cycles, emphasizing the principle of time-based calculation over biological markers. The hadith underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on divorce, ensuring clarity in marital status transitions.
